mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which reduces earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -1% and HOUST < -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST decline by more than 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 3% during a recession signals a monetary policy easing intended to stimulate growth, which typically precedes a recovery in risk assets and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS falls below 3% and UNRATE exceeds 5% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 0.5% in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals accelerating demand growth, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 0.5% and RSAFS > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and RSAFS rise by more than 0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.3% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of four consecutive months with PAYEMS growth above 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.4% for three consecutive months signals improving supply conditions and economic momentum, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of three consecutive months with INDPRO growth above 0.4%.
